design.howItWorksIntro: This guide summarizes the full design flow so you can place pieces, validate support and review the final volume without losing context.

howItWorks.title: Choose a piece
howItWorks.text: Pick a block, pillar or accessory from the side panel.

howItWorks.title: Edit in 2D
howItWorks.text: Place pieces on the plan and switch floors whenever you need to.

howItWorks.title: Visualize in 3D
howItWorks.text: Review the built volume with the three-dimensional view.

guide2d.title: 2D guide
guide2d.intro: The 2D plan is where you build the logic of the project before seeing the final volume.

sections.title: 1. Choose the right piece
sections.text: Select a block, pillar or accessory from the sidebar and check the material, type and active floor before placing it.

sections.title: 2. Place and correct on the plan
sections.text: Click on the board to place the piece. If you hold the button, you can paint several points in a row; if you change your mind, delete with the same logic.

sections.title: 3. Respect support rules
sections.text: The editor validates whether a piece needs support below, a lateral connection or to be on floor 0 so that nothing floats or is poorly anchored.

sections.title: 4. Switch floors when needed
sections.text: Go up and down in height to review each layer of the project. That way you can adjust gaps, check overlaps and work section by section.

sections.title: 5. Use quick actions
sections.text: Undo, redo, save, load, export and move the board are designed so you can iterate without wasting time.

sections.title: 6. Review the preview
sections.text: The plan shows a preview when the cursor hovers over it, so you know before confirming whether placement is valid or not.

guide2d.footer: Tip: if in doubt, work in 2D first until the overall piece layout is closed and use 3D only to check proportions and height.

guide3d.title: 3D guide
guide3d.intro: The 3D view turns the plan into a more intuitive spatial reading to understand the final result.

sections.title: 1. Look at the full volume
sections.text: Each piece becomes a volumetric block with its real height, making the final form of the whole easier to understand.

sections.title: 2. Read the visible layers
sections.text: Height guides and the three-dimensional grid help you understand which layers are active and how much volume has been accumulated.

sections.title: 3. Distinguish structure and accessories
sections.text: Structural elements feel more solid, while accessories are shown more lightly to make reading easier.

sections.title: 4. Compare measurements and proportions
sections.text: Dimension guides and the volume outline let you check width, depth and height with a fast visual reference.

sections.title: 5. Adjust the camera
sections.text: Rotate, zoom in and zoom out to inspect the project from different viewpoints without losing spatial orientation.

sections.title: 6. Use 3D as final validation
sections.text: When the 2D plan is already solved, 3D helps confirm that the overall composition, heights and supports make sense.

guide3d.footer: Tip: go back to the 2D plan if you find a layer that does not fit; the 3D view is meant as the final design check.

about.title: Our story
about.intro1: SquareStruct was born in the classroom, but looks toward real construction: a simple way to explore, compare and plan modular solutions before building.
about.intro2: We want choosing stackable materials to feel clear and approachable, where every piece has a purpose inside the project the user imagines.
about.intro3: Behind the platform there is practice, learning and teamwork: an academic idea turned into a useful tool to solve concrete needs.

raul.name: Raúl Martín
raul.bio: Raúl is passionate about video games and technology. He focused his training on systems and web development from his first steps, aiming to apply what he learned in real projects.

cristian.name: Cristian Gil
cristian.bio: Cristian reinvented his career toward the technology sector. He focused his learning on web development and brings a practical background in systems and networks, aiming to create useful solutions for real projects.
